411:         GLOBAL_CONSTRAINT_CODE[global_constraint],
412:         sakoe_chiba_radius,
413:         itakura_max_slope,
414:         be=be,
415:     )
416:     if be.is_numpy:
417:         acc_cost_mat = njit_accumulated_matrix(s1, s2, mask=mask)
418:         path = _njit_return_path(acc_cost_mat)
419:     else:
420:         acc_cost_mat = accumulated_matrix(s1, s2, mask=mask, be=be)
421:         path = _return_path(acc_cost_mat, be=be)
422:     return path, be.sqrt(acc_cost_mat[-1, -1])
423: 
424: 
425: @njit()
426: def njit_accumulated_matrix_from_dist_matrix(dist_matrix, mask):
427:     """Compute the accumulated cost matrix score between two time series using
428:     a precomputed distance matrix.
429: 
430:     Parameters
431:     ----------
432:     dist_matrix : array-like, shape=(sz1, sz2)
433:         Array containing the pairwise distances.
434:     mask : array-like, shape=(sz1, sz2)
435:         Mask. Unconsidered cells must have False values.
436: 
437:     Returns
438:     -------
439:     mat : array-like, shape=(sz1, sz2)
440:         Accumulated cost matrix.
441:     """
442:     l1, l2 = dist_matrix.shape
443:     cum_sum = numpy.full((l1 + 1, l2 + 1), numpy.inf)
444:     cum_sum[0, 0] = 0.0
445: 
446:     for i in prange(l1):
447:         for j in prange(l2):
448:             if mask[i, j]:
449:                 cum_sum[i + 1, j + 1] = dist_matrix[i, j]
450:                 cum_sum[i + 1, j + 1] += min(
451:                     cum_sum[i, j + 1], cum_sum[i + 1, j], cum_sum[i, j]
452:                 )
453:     return cum_sum[1:, 1:]
454: 
455: 
456: def accumulated_matrix_from_dist_matrix(dist_matrix, mask, be=None):
457:     """Compute the accumulated cost matrix score between two time series using
458:     a precomputed distance matrix.
459: 
460:     Parameters
461:     ----------
462:     dist_matrix : array-like, shape=(sz1, sz2)
463:         Array containing the pairwise distances.
464:     mask : array-like, shape=(sz1, sz2)
465:         Mask. Unconsidered cells must have False values.
466:     be : Backend object or string or None
467:         Backend. If `be` is an instance of the class `NumPyBackend` or the string `"numpy"`,
468:         the NumPy backend is used.
469:         If `be` is an instance of the class `PyTorchBackend` or the string `"pytorch"`,
470:         the PyTorch backend is used.
471:         If `be` is `None`, the backend is determined by the input arrays.
472:         See our :ref:`dedicated user-guide page <backend>` for more information.
473: 
474:     Returns
475:     -------
476:     mat : array-like, shape=(sz1, sz2)
477:         Accumulated cost matrix.
478:     """
479:     be = instantiate_backend(be, dist_matrix)
480:     dist_matrix = be.array(dist_matrix)
481:     l1, l2 = be.shape(dist_matrix)
482:     cum_sum = be.full((l1 + 1, l2 + 1), be.inf)
483:     cum_sum[0, 0] = 0.0
484: 
485:     for i in range(l1):
486:         for j in range(l2):
487:             if mask[i, j]:
488:                 cum_sum[i + 1, j + 1] = dist_matrix[i, j]
489:                 cum_sum[i + 1, j + 1] += min(
490:                     cum_sum[i, j + 1], cum_sum[i + 1, j], cum_sum[i, j]
491:                 )
492:     return cum_sum[1:, 1:]
493: 
494: 
495: def dtw_path_from_metric(
496:     s1,
497:     s2=None,
498:     metric="euclidean",
499:     global_constraint=None,
500:     sakoe_chiba_radius=None,
501:     itakura_max_slope=None,
502:     be=None,
503:     **kwds
504: ):
505:     r"""Compute Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) similarity measure between
506:     (possibly multidimensional) time series using a distance metric defined by
507:     the user and return both the path and the similarity.
508: 
509:     Similarity is computed as the cumulative cost along the aligned time
510:     series.
511: 
512:     It is not required that both time series share the same size, but they must
513:     be the same dimension. DTW was originally presented in [1]_.
514: 
515:     Valid values for metric are the same as for scikit-learn
516:     `pairwise_distances`_ function i.e. a string (e.g. "euclidean",
517:     "sqeuclidean", "hamming") or a function that is used to compute the
518:     pairwise distances. See `scikit`_ and `scipy`_ documentations for more
519:     information about the available metrics.
520: 
521:     Parameters
522:     ----------
523:     s1 : array-like, shape=(sz1, d) or (sz1,) if metric!="precomputed", (sz1, sz2) otherwise
524:         A time series or an array of pairwise distances between samples.
525:         If shape is (sz1,), the time series is assumed to be univariate.
526: 
527:     s2 : array-like, shape=(sz2, d) or (sz2,), optional (default: None)
528:         A second time series, only allowed if metric != "precomputed".
529:         If shape is (sz2,), the time series is assumed to be univariate.
530: 
531:     metric : string or callable (default: "euclidean")
532:         Function used to compute the pairwise distances between each points of
533:         `s1` and `s2`.
534: 
535:         If metric is "precomputed", `s1` is assumed to be a distance matrix.
536: 
537:         If metric is an other string, it must be one of the options compatible
538:         with sklearn.metrics.pairwise_distances.
539: 
540:         Alternatively, if metric is a callable function, it is called on pairs
541:         of rows of `s1` and `s2`. The callable should take two 1 dimensional
542:         arrays as input and return a value indicating the distance between
543:         them.
544: 
545:     global_constraint : {"itakura", "sakoe_chiba"} or None (default: None)
546:         Global constraint to restrict admissible paths for DTW.
547: 
548:     sakoe_chiba_radius : int or None (default: None)
549:         Radius to be used for Sakoe-Chiba band global constraint.
550:         The Sakoe-Chiba radius corresponds to the parameter :math:`\delta` mentioned in [1]_,
551:         it controls how far in time we can go in order to match a given
552:         point from one time series to a point in another time series.
553:         If None and `global_constraint` is set to "sakoe_chiba", a radius of
554:         1 is used.
555:         If both `sakoe_chiba_radius` and `itakura_max_slope` are set,
556:         `global_constraint` is used to infer which constraint to use among the
557:         two. In this case, if `global_constraint` corresponds to no global
558:         constraint, a `RuntimeWarning` is raised and no global constraint is
559:         used.
560: 
561:     itakura_max_slope : float or None (default: None)
562:         Maximum slope for the Itakura parallelogram constraint.
563:         If None and `global_constraint` is set to "itakura", a maximum slope
564:         of 2. is used.
565:         If both `sakoe_chiba_radius` and `itakura_max_slope` are set,
566:         `global_constraint` is used to infer which constraint to use among the
